$comment: Every route the vendored WOO bundle (build/woo) answers, read out of its own build output, and where each one lives once the bundle is gone (retire-the-vendored-woo-bundle, tasks 3 and 4). `tests/woo-bundle-routes.spec.mjs` extracts the set from build/woo/static/js and fails when a route is missing here, so the set is enumerated rather than sampled. kind: `page` is a page of lib/Settings/sites/open-publicaties.json; `auth` is the portal's own sign-in edge (DigiD, eHerkenning), never a bundled screen; `own-area` is the authenticated portal at /mijn with its contribution aggregate; `out-of-scope` carries the reason it is not carried over.

routes.reason: The index of the registration forms below; with none of them carried over there is nothing to list.

Registering an application in the software catalogue is stackiq's. Its portal contribution declares read collections only and defers create-actions (stackiq design), so there is no contribution action to point at yet.
Service self-registration is one of the create-actions stackiq's portal contribution defers; it comes back as that action, not as a portaliq page.
Registering a link between applications is stackiq data entry; stackiq's portal contribution offers no create-action for it.
Registering a product is stackiq data entry; stackiq's portal contribution offers no create-action for it.
Recording use of a catalogue entry is stackiq's; its portal contribution reads use (vendorGebruik, participantGebruik) but writes none.

Registering an organisation is a stackiq form (organisation-registration, sourceApp stackiq), which a site that installs stackiq declares, as the Zuiddrecht site does; this generic publication site does not ship it.
Administration: it belongs in the admin interface behind Nextcloud sign-in, never on a public origin (proposal, non-goals).
